source.title: Investigating Model Editing for Unlearning in Large Language Models

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies model-editing methods as unlearning interventions and measures forgetting and retained utility. It does not test recovery attacks, so it bears only on the forgetting-and-utility portion of version A.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates forgetting on TOFU and reports retained-utility metrics, but does not fine-tune unlearned models to recover facts, ablate an activation direction, quantize weights, or test prompt-based recovery. It also does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance: Forget Quality is based on a distribution comparison with the ground-truth unlearned model. The paper cites rephrased-query and hidden-state extraction attacks by Patil et al.; those are not this study's results. Table 2 is flattened in the supplied text, so numeric assignments to individual editing conditions are not sufficiently clear to extract.
record.test_reason: It applies model-editing methods (ROME, IKE, WISE) as unlearning on TOFU with Llama-2-7B. Its own results show whether forgetting (Forget Quality vs a retain-only model) coexists with retained utility, which bears on the first half of A. Appendix Table 9 also scores edits on paraphrased forget questions, a benign rephrasing check relevant to E. No recovery attacks are run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim editing (ROME Dummy, IKE Incorrect) can exceed TOFU's baseline unlearning methods in Forget Quality, and that most target-algorithm settings fail to reach the ground-truth distribution. Where forgetting does succeed, it costs out-of-scope performance. The best choice of algorithm and target depends on the use case. They also note IKE leaves latent knowledge accessible since weights are unchanged.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates ROME, IKE, and WISE as editing-based unlearning methods on TOFU; it does not reproduce the recovery attacks or unlearning methods named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by editing algorithm and target definition; ROME degrades with the more complex Incorrect and Avoidant targets, while WISE has higher utility but weak forgetting.

fits_no_version.finding: Editing-based unlearning on TOFU shows algorithm- and target-dependent trade-offs between Forget Quality and Model Utility.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-editing methods can match a retain-only model's forget distribution in some target settings, but usually at a utility cost or with failed forgetting.

record.peer_reviewed: COLM 2025 Workshop: Socially Responsible Language Modelling Research (SoLaR)
record.problems: The study uses one model, Llama-2-7B, and fictitious TOFU data. It uses baseline results supplied by Maini et al. rather than rerunning those methods. The supplied Table 2 text is flattened, making individual numeric assignments unclear. No recovery attack is evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2's individual component metrics (ROUGE, Probability, Truth Ratio) and baseline values are not extracted because the flattened layout does not reliably assign all values to methods and conditions. Appendix Tables 9–11 report editing reliability, generalization, and locality metrics, but these assess edit performance rather than recovery of unlearned knowledge.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the edited knowledge; accuracy against chance.
No activation ablation or hidden-state probing. The authors only argue that IKE leaves latent knowledge accessible because weights are unchanged.
No jailbreaks, other languages or adversarial prompts. Only benign paraphrases of edited prompts are tested (Table 9).
No method is claimed or tested to resist recovery attacks.

missing.what: IKE Dummy Forget Quality 4.91E-20 (MU 0.338) and IKE Avoidant Forget Quality 2.43E-17 (MU 0.452): both fail the threshold.
Generalization on paraphrased forget questions: Dummy ROME 0.975, IKE 1.0, WISE 0.0425; Incorrect IKE 0.983; Avoidant IKE 0.997.

Exact Table 2 values are recoverable despite flattening (14 columns: GT, 3 editors × 3 targets, KL, GA, GD, PO). Baseline unlearning Forget Quality ranges 1.43E-22 to 5.10E-17; these are taken from Maini et al. and should be marked as cited, not new.

record.verdict_notes: Single model (Llama-2-7B) and fictitious TOFU data. Baselines and the ground truth are not rerun. Forget Quality is a distribution test, not chance-level accuracy. IKE is an in-context method, so 'unlearning' via IKE is prompt-level and arguably not weight unlearning. The E evidence is weak: the paraphrases are benign, not adversarial.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures forgetting and general utility, but not targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance or whether simple attacks recover the knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether knowledge is deleted versus inaccessible.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test after unlearning.
No method is evaluated for resisting the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

rows.check: The values are readable: WISE Forget Quality is 4.22E-21 (Dummy), 8.99E-07 (Incorrect) and 2.43E-17 (Avoidant). Model Utility is about 0.60–0.61.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B
rows.operation_detail: ROME edits using Incorrect and Avoidant targets on Forget 10
rows.value: ROME failed to produce outputs for many inputs; example outputs are described as gibberish
rows.note: The authors treat this as substantial degradation of general model performance, rather than successful targeted forgetting.
rows.check: ROME Incorrect/Avoidant produce gibberish or no output, and Table 2 metrics are missing ('-'). Locality is 0.043 and 0.029 (Tables 10–11). Neither the forgetting nor the retained ability is achieved; this is degeneration, so absent rather than partial.

relationships.reason: Forget Quality 0.121 passes the threshold, but Model Utility drops to 0.153 vs 0.614, so general ability is not kept (r1, r2).
relationships.display_finding: Forget Quality reached 0.121, but Model Utility fell from 0.614 to 0.153.

relationships.condition: IKE, Incorrect target (in-context, no weight change)
relationships.reason: Forget Quality 0.249 passes the threshold, but utility falls to 0.473 vs 0.614. This is the only near-success, and it comes with a utility cost (r3, r4).
relationships.display_finding: Forget quality reached 0.249 and passed the threshold, while utility fell from 0.614 to 0.473.

relationships.reason: Forget Quality is at most 8.99E-07, far below 0.05; edits are not applied at generation (r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Forget Quality stayed at or below 8.99E-07 against a 0.05 threshold because edits were not applied during generation.
